subject: Service surge — CEO-level briefing requested
messages:
From: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@lumenhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lumen Health Engineering <ops@lumen.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 08:45:12 -0700
Subject: Unexpected latency spike affecting inference calls

Jordan —

We started seeing a large spike in tail latency across our inference traffic at ~08:20 PT. Around 6-8% of requests are timing out (~5s+), and fallbacks to our cached responses are happening. This is impacting critical user workflows for two of our product flows (auth and recommendations).

Request IDs showing errors: req_3f9a, req_3fb2, req_3fd8.

Ops has already routed traffic to a lower-capacity region but we need clarity on root cause and when we can expect normal latencies to return. Our CTO is asking for an executive-level summary and a clear ETA for restoration for his leadership call at 13:00 PT.

Can you please escalate and provide a short exec note we can share internally? Any visibility on scope, rollback or mitigations is appreciated.

— Sarah
Sarah Cho
CTO — Lumen Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 08:53:07 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected latency spike affecting inference calls

Team — starting a rapid bridge. Notifying on-call infra and runtime leads now. High-level plan:

1) Confirm whether this is a serving runtime regression or regional capacity exhaustion (owner: Ben).
2) If runtime regression, rollback to v12 kernels and force use of smaller batch windows (owner: Marissa).
3) Provide per-customer impact summary and traffic split so we can tailor comms to Lumen (owner: Jordan).
4) Exec note copy: we need a 2–3 sentence customer-facing summary + commitments (ETA, credit/comp offer).

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv (initial timeline I'm assembling)

Action items: Ben, can you confirm first-seen metric and whether a kernel change deployed ~08:10? Marissa, confirm whether autoscaler showed a backlog and whether we can spin a dedicated pool. I will draft the exec note and loop in legal if we recommend credits.

I will post the bridge link in #ops-bridge in 2 minutes.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 09:02:41 -07:00
Subject: RE: RE: Unexpected latency spike affecting inference calls

Short answers first: we saw a kernel rollout to v14 at 08:09 PT across two clusters; one cluster experienced degraded memory pressure leading to slower KV cache reads. That explains the 08:20 tail latency spike.

Current status: rollback-in-progress to v12 on the affected cluster. Autoscaler did spike but backed off when we throttled batching — backlog reduced by ~60% in the last 12 minutes.

For the exec note, propose the following language (very short):

"What happened: We experienced an unexpected runtime regression during a kernel rollout that increased tail latency for a subset of requests.

Impact: Approximately 6–8% of requests for your account experienced elevated latency or timeouts between 08:10–08:40 PT; normal service was restored for most traffic by 09:00 PT.

What we’re doing: We rolled back the recent kernel change, are validating stability, and will provide a full timeline and remediation plan within 48 hours. We will also issue a credit for affected requests."

Questions for Jordan: can you confirm the exact window Lumen saw (we have aggregate metrics but need per-customer alignment)?

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Reliability Engineer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 09:14:58 -07:00
Subject: RE: RE: RE: Unexpected latency spike affecting inference calls

Confirming Ben's notes. Also:

- Technically: the affected kernel path increases KV cache lookups per-token under certain quantization profiles; fallback path caused GC pressure. We're running an extended validation suite now.
- SLA: marginal breach risk for 08:10–08:35 window for premium SLAs.
- Recommendation for customer-facing note: soften the language, emphasize early mitigation and that we're issuing a one-time credit. Add an explicit ETA for the postmortem (48 hours) and a follow-up remediation timeline (2 weeks for patch + 4-week monitoring).

Proposed short customer note (slightly edited):

"Summary: This morning we observed a regression during a runtime kernel rollout that transiently increased latency for a subset of inference requests. Our engineers rolled back the change and performed targeted mitigations; normal performance was restored by ~09:00 PT for most traffic.

Next steps: We will provide a detailed incident timeline and remediation plan within 48 hours and deploy a permanent fix in the coming two weeks. We will also issue a credit for impacted requests and keep you updated daily until the fix is confirmed.

We apologize for the disruption and are prioritizing stability for your critical flows."

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Reliability

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@lumenhealth.com>, Lumen Health Engineering <ops@lumen.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 13:30:05 -07:00
Subject: Service disruption summary and immediate commitments (Lumen Health)

Sarah —

Thank you for flagging this quickly and for your patience while we worked to stabilize the service. Below is a concise executive summary you can share with leadership:

Short summary (for execs):
- What happened: During a kernel rollout at ~08:09 PT we introduced a regression that increased tail latency for a subset of inference requests.
- Impact: Approximately 6–8% of requests for Lumen Health experienced elevated latency or timeouts between ~08:10–08:40 PT. Most traffic returned to expected performance by ~09:00 PT; a small portion of traffic required re-routing to an adjacent region.
- What we did: We rolled back the kernel change, throttled batching to relieve GC pressure, and reduced backlog via autoscaler interventions.
- Commitments:
  1) Full incident timeline and root cause analysis within 48 hours (drive link below).
  2) Permanent kernel fix and validation within two weeks; extended monitoring for 4 weeks after deployment.
  3) One-time account credit covering affected requests; our billing team will follow up with specifics.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/incident/LP-20280719-lumen (contains incident-timeline.csv and customer-impact-summary.pdf)
HubSpot: HUB-987654

Immediate asks we need from your side: a list of the two product flows we should prioritize in the remediation testing (you mentioned auth and recommendations earlier).

Again, we’re sorry for the disruption. I will personally own daily updates until the remediation is deployed and validated. If you’d like a 15-minute briefing before your 13:00 PT leadership call, I’m available at 12:45 PT; otherwise please use the drive doc for the latest raw metrics.

-Jordan Blake
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: customer-impact-summary.pdf (attached)
